claim_checks.evidence: UV FILTERS: CONFIRMED exactly. Official srichand.com INCI for Sunlution Acne Care lists Butyl Methoxydibenzoylmethane (pos 2), Ethylhexyl Salicylate (3), Ethylhexyl Triazone (4), Diethylamino Hydroxybenzoyl Hexyl Benzoate (9), Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine (15), Titanium Dioxide (18) - no other filters. Order-identical on Watsons, Skinsort and one INCIDecoder listing. OTHER ACTIVES: REFUTED. Niacinamide, 3-O-Ethyl Ascorbic Acid, Tocopherol and Palmitoyl Tetrapeptide-10 are NOT in Acne Care - they belong to Sunlution Skin Whitening. The error comes from a mis-uploaded INCIDecoder listing ('Srichand Sunlution Acne Care Sunscreen SPF50+/pa++++', user upload 07/10/2022) that is a verbatim copy of the Whitening list; it is the first hit in web search. Silica is correct (pos 6). What Acne Care really has instead: Gluconolactone (23), Tocopheryl Acetate (24), Salicylic Acid (32), 3 ceramides, Ascorbic Acid (42), Palmitoyl Tripeptide-5 (52). SALICYLIC ACID: YES, present at position 32 of 54 - consistent with the official 'Salicylic Acid Sphere' claim, but it sits deep in the list (below Phenoxyethanol at 11 and Chlorphenesin at 17), so the level is low; % not disclosed.

'Hybrid': CONFIRMED from official INCI - 5 organic filters (avobenzone, octisalate, ethylhexyl triazone, DHHB, bemotrizinol) + Titanium Dioxide. 'Fragrance-free': CONFIRMED by ingredient analysis - no Parfum/Fragrance or essential oils among the 40 ingredients; Skinsort tags it Fragrance-free and Alcohol-free. However srichand.com does not itself make a fragrance-free claim for this product. 'Matte finish': NOT a brand claim - it is Skinsort's auto-generated blurb ('Hybrid sunscreen with a matte finish that helps control shine'). The brand's own wording is 'Micro-blur Primer: absorbs oil, blurs lines/pores', lightweight, usable in place of make-up base - directionally consistent but never says 'matte'. Also: Skinsort does NOT tag this product reef-safe or silicone-free (it contains Dimethicone).
SUMMARY: the hero/heritage statement is wrong; 'purple' is true of the packaging but not of the powder; the Skinsort tags are quoted correctly but are weak evidence. See c-1, c-2, c-3.

claim_checks.claim: c-1 (Bare to Perfect is the brand's heritage hero)
claim_checks.evidence: The famous hero is the classic 'Srichand Translucent Powder' (10 g / 30 g), launched May 2014 as the centrepiece of the rebrand (Bangkok Post, 'Rebranding brings return to success'); Watsons describes it as 'Award winning and one of the best-selling facial powders in Thailand'. 'Bare to Perfect Translucent Powder' is a separate, later line (12-h 'Sebum Sensor' oil control, Soft Focus, EXO-P anti-pollution; sifter + thick puff) with a completely different formula (32-ingredient talc/mica/silica list vs the classic's blend-style list). They are two different SKUs sold side by side on srichand.com.

claim_checks.claim: c-2 (the purple powder they're known for)
claim_checks.evidence: PACKAGING (official product images on srichand.com viewed 2026-09-18): the classic Translucent Powder has a deep/dark purple lid covered in a multicolour floral-and-bird illustration with gold line art; Bare to Perfect Translucent Powder has a plain bright-violet lid with tonal embossed flowers and a white SRICHAND wordmark. Both are shot against purple roses/purple powder bursts, i.e. purple is the brand colour for BOTH. I could not verify a 'black box' for the classic - a reseller describes it as 'Classic Dark Purple with Gold Lettering' and Bare to Perfect as 'Light Purple with Gold Lettering'; the dark purple can read as black. POWDER COLOUR: neither powder is purple. Bare to Perfect Translucent is tinted only with iron oxides (CI 77492/77491/77499); the classic with CI19140, CI77120, CI77491, CI77492. The only genuinely purple-toned powder is 'Bare to Perfect Correcting Loose Powder 12 g', a 4-colour powder (pink-purple-peach-blue, may contain CI 77007, CI 73360). So: say 'purple packaging', not 'purple powder', and attach 'known for' to the classic.

claim_checks.claim: c-3 (reef-safe and fungal-acne-safe per third-party analysis)
claim_checks.evidence: Skinsort's page for 'Srichand Bare To Perfect Translucent Powder' (32 ingredients, updated 15 Dec 2025) does show active tags 'Reef-safe' and 'Fungal-acne-safe' (plus alcohol-, fragrance-, oil-, paraben-, sulfate-free; NOT silicone-free, NOT tagged vegan/cruelty-free). CAVEATS: these are algorithmic ingredient-screen tags, not test results; 'reef-safe' is irrelevant for a face powder with no UV filters and is not worth quoting; the same INCI contains Talc and Perfluorooctyl Triethoxysilane (a fluorinated/PFAS-class coating), which a 'clean' framing would invite scrutiny of.

STATUS ON 2026-09-18: (1) Bemotrizinol (Tinosorb S, INCI Bis-Ethylhexyloxyphenol Methoxyphenyl Triazine) is NOW PERMITTED in the US. FDA proposed it in Dec 2025 (Federal Register 12 Dec 2025, docket FDA-2025-N-6494) and FINALISED it: FDA press release dated June 09, 2026 - 'Today, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration added bemotrizinol to the list of permitted sunscreen active ingredients... The agency reviewed public comments on the proposed order and is now issuing the final order.' Final administrative order OTC000039, published in the Federal Register 10 June 2026; GRASE at up to 6% for adults and children 6 months+; effective 9 August 2026 (effective date per CIRS/regulatory summaries, not stated in the FDA press release). First new US sunscreen active since the late 1990s. (2) DHHB (Uvinul A Plus) - NOT permitted: not in OTC Monograph M020. (3) Ethylhexyl Triazone (Uvinul T 150 / octyl triazone) - NOT permitted: not in M020. FDA's consumer sunscreen page (content current as of 09/10/2026) lists the permitted actives including bemotrizinol and does not list DHHB, ethylhexyl triazone, bisoctrizole or iscotrizinol. VERDICT ON THE DRAFT SENTENCE: 'two of those filters aren't permitted in the US' is numerically TRUE today ONLY if the two are DHHB and ethylhexyl triazone; if the draft counted Tinosorb S as one of them it is out of date (before 9 Jun 2026 the count was three). Wording fix: FDA does not 'approve for sale' monograph sunscreen ingredients - say 'not permitted as sunscreen active ingredients under the US FDA OTC monograph'. Wider context: other Srichand/SASI SPF products use further non-US filters - MBBT/bisoctrizole (Rosia, Tone Up, SASI Acne Sol, both liquid foundations), Diethylhexyl Butamido Triazone/iscotrizinol (Moisture Burst Watery), Isoamyl p-Methoxycinnamate/amiloxate (SASI sunscreens, Super Fix, old Fine Smooth Foundation).
